messages.author: a3ea45e87285d820
messages.subject: Re: gl.filter.callrate / gl.filter.monomorphs error
parts:
Hi Walter,

Bringing data in from non DArT sources is likely to lead to glitches. The problem arises because dartR genlight objects have additional information embedded in them. Your best option is to run

gl2 <- gl.compatability.check(gl)

which will check the structure of the genlight object and correct if necessary.

You will need to be running the latest version available from github -- see postings below.

A

messages.author: a3ea45e87285d820
messages.subject: Re: gl.filter.callrate / gl.filter.monomorphs error
parts:
Sorry Walter,

If you download the latest version of dartR as per the instructions earlier in these postings, it should be there. Did you use:

install.packages("leaflet.
providers")
install.packages("lifecycle")
install.packages("farver")
install_github("green-striped-gecko/dartR", ref="dev") # no need to upgrade prior installs, answer no.

I am not sure what happened, but I have included the script here. You could just run that script, then run gl.compliance.check(), but would be best to install as above and run it in context.

Did not help that I had the name wrong. gl.compliance.check, not gl.compatability.check. My bad.

A

messages.author: b3d929c6746ca81a
messages.subject: RE: [dartR] Re: gl.filter.callrate / gl.filter.monomorphs error
parts:
Hi Walter,

 

you need to use the development version as the latest version is not on cran yet.

 

So as Arthur mentioned before, use:
install_github("green-striped-gecko/dartR", ref="dev") # no need to upgrade prior installs, answer no.

You can check the version installed via:

 

> packageVersion("dartR")

[1] ‘1.5.5’

 

And then you should have the compliance function.

 

 

Cheers, Bernd
